title: Translating
summary: Translating and interpreting is the general heading for translation technique. --Translating is free-floating (topical) under individual languages and language groups, disciplines, and topical headings (for translating services in a field); --Translating into [name of language] under languages (two headings if both directions); --Machine translating under languages, with Machine translating as the general heading. Translating services is the general heading for translating organizations, with specific headings for court, deaf, congress, international agency and UN services. Sacred works: see H 1300.
validation_rules: `Translating and interpreting` is the heading for general works on methods and tools of translating and interpreting. (H 2219 sec. D.1)
`--Translating` is a free-floating topical subdivision under individual languages and language groups, e.g. `English language--Translating`. (H 2219 sec. D.2.a)

`--Translating into [name of language]` is free-floating under individual languages or language groups, e.g. `English language--Translating into German`; for both directions assign two headings (e.g. also `German language--Translating into English`). (H 2219 sec. D.2.b)

`--Translating` is free-floating under disciplines, e.g. `Science--Translating`, `Poetry--Translating`, and under topical headings for organizations providing translating services in a field, e.g. `Technology--Translating`. (H 2219 sec. D.3, F.3)
`--Translating` under sacred works is governed by H 1300 (e.g. `Bible--Translating`, `Bible. Old Testament. Ethiopic--Translating`). (H 2219 sec. D.4, G)

`Machine translating` is the heading for general works; `--Machine translating` is free-floating under individual languages and language groups, e.g. `German language--Machine translating`, with a second heading `[language]--Translating into [language]` for the target language. (H 2219 sec. E)

`Translating services` is the heading for general works on translating organizations; specialized services take `Court interpreting and translating`, `Interpreters for deaf people`, `Congresses and conventions--Translating services`, `International agencies--Translating services`, `United Nations--Translating services`. (H 2219 sec. F.1-F.2)
Translations themselves are governed by H 2220, not by `--Translating`. (H 2219 sec. A)

[LC practice] LC does not use form subdivisions; assign LCGFT terms (e.g. `Handbooks and manuals`) and, where a form subdivision would include a demographic group, LCDGT terms (e.g. `German speakers`, `Arabic, Students of`). (H 2219 sec. A)

sections.heading: A. Background
sections.text:
The heading *Translating and interpreting* and the subdivision *--Translating* are assigned to works that discuss the technique of translating from one language to another. The heading *Machine translating* and the subdivision *--Machine translating* are assigned to works about the process of translating from one language to another by computer. The heading *Translating services* and the subdivisions *--Translating* and *--Translating services* are assigned to works on the services offered by organizations specializing in translating and interpreting. This instruction sheet provides guidelines for assigning these headings and subdivisions. For guidelines on translations, see H 2220.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Handbooks and manuals*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.

sections.heading: B. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-02: Updated template. Added alternative instructions for LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: C. Definitions
sections.text:
Translation: an act, process, or instance of translating, such as a rendering from one language into another[^1]; in general, translation applies to written texts and interpretation applies to oral communication.

[^1]: TRANSLATION Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster

sections.heading: D.1. General
sections.text: Assign the heading *Translating and interpreting* to general works on the methods, tools, etc., used to render texts or oral communication from a language or languages into other languages.

sections.heading: D.2.a. General
sections.text: Assign the free-floating topical subdivision *--Translating* under individual languages and language groups for works on the techniques, tools, etc., of translating texts or oral communication in these languages, for example, *English language--Translating*.

sections.heading: D.2.b. Translating into French, [German, etc.]
sections.text:
Assign the free-floating subdivision *--Translating into [name of language]* under individual languages or language groups for works on methods of translating a language or language group into another specific language. If the work discusses translating in both directions, assign two headings.

Example:

```
Title: English-German translating.
650 #0 $a English language $x Translating into German.
650 #0 $a German language $x Translating into English.
```

sections.heading: D.3. Disciplines
sections.text: Assign the free-floating subdivision *--Translating* under disciplines for works on the techniques, tools, etc., of translating works on these subjects, for example, *Science--Translating*.

sections.heading: D.4. Sacred works
sections.text: For instructions on assigning the subdivision *--Translating* under sacred works, see H 1300.

sections.heading: E.1. General
sections.text: Assign the heading *Machine translating* to general works discussing the process of translating texts from one language to another by computer.

sections.heading: E.2. Special languages
sections.text:
Assign the free-floating subdivision *--Machine translating* under individual languages and language groups for works on the technique of translating texts in that language by computer. If the work discusses methods of machine translating into a specific language, assign a second heading to bring out the language into which materials are being translated.

Example:

```
Title: Some problems in German to English machine translations.
650 #0 $a German language $x Machine translating.
650 #0 $a German language $x Translating into English.
```

sections.heading: F.1. General
sections.text: Assign the heading *Translating services* to general works on organizations that specialize in providing translating and interpreting services.

sections.heading: F.2. Special services
sections.text: Assign the headings *Court interpreting and translating*, *Interpreters for deaf people*, *Congresses and conventions--Translating services*, *International agencies--Translating services*, and *United Nations--Translating services* to works that discuss these specialized translating and interpreting services.

sections.heading: F.3. Special fields
sections.text: Assign the free-floating subdivision *--Translating* under topical headings to works on organizations that provide translating and interpreting services in specific fields, for example, *Technology--Translating*.

sections.heading: G. Extended examples
sections.text:
```
Title: Translating a worldview : linguistic worldview in literary translation.
650 #0 $a Poetry $x Translating.

Title: Scientific and technical translation.
650 #0 $a Technology $x Translating.
650 #0 $a Science $x Translating.

Title: Translating the Bible : the Ethiopic version of the Old Testament.
630 00 $a Bible $x Translating.
630 00 $a Bible. $p Old Testament. $l Ethiopic $x Translating.
650 #0 $a Ethiopic language $x Translating.
```
